reagents.name: LiAlH4 (Lithium Aluminium Hydride)
reagents.function: Powerful non-selective reducing agent; reduces aldehydes, ketones, esters, carboxylic acids, acyl chlorides, and amides to alcohols/amines in dry ether.

reagents.name: NaBH4 (Sodium Borohydride)
reagents.function: Mild selective reducing agent in protic solvents (methanol/ethanol); reduces aldehydes and ketones to 1° and 2° alcohols while leaving esters and acids untouched.

reagents.name: PCC (Pyridinium Chlorochromate)
reagents.function: Selective mild oxidant in anhydrous CH2Cl2; oxidises 1° alcohols to aldehydes (avoids over-oxidation to carboxylic acids) and 2° alcohols to ketones.

reagents.name: PDC (Pyridinium Dichromate)
reagents.function: Oxidising agent; oxidises 1° alcohols to aldehydes in CH2Cl2 or to carboxylic acids in DMF; oxidises 2° alcohols cleanly to ketones.

reagents.name: Jones Reagent (CrO3 / aqueous H2SO4 / Acetone)
reagents.function: Strong primary oxidant; rapidly oxidises 1° alcohols to carboxylic acids and 2° alcohols to ketones via chromic acid intermediates.

reagents.name: KMnO4 (Hot Alkaline / Acidic)
reagents.function: Vigorous oxidant; cleaves alkenes/alkynes into ketones/carboxylic acids and oxidises alkylbenzene side chains with benzylic hydrogens into benzoic acid.
reagents.example: Toluene (PhCH3) + KMnO4 / KOH, heat, then H3O+ -> PhCOOH

reagents.name: Baeyer's Reagent (Cold dilute alkaline KMnO4)
reagents.function: Syn-1,2-dihydroxylation reagent for alkenes; adds two OH groups to the same face of a double bond with decolourisation of purple KMnO4.

reagents.name: OsO4 (Osmium Tetroxide / NMO or H2O2)
reagents.function: Stereospecific syn-dihydroxylation of alkenes via cyclic osmate ester intermediate to yield vicinal cis-diols.

reagents.name: O3 followed by Zn / H2O (Reductive Ozonolysis)
reagents.function: Cleaves carbon-carbon double bonds to form aldehydes and ketones cleanly without over-oxidation to carboxylic acids.

reagents.name: O3 followed by H2O2 (Oxidative Ozonolysis)
reagents.function: Cleaves alkenes oxidatively; converts aldehydic fragments into carboxylic acids and ketonic fragments into ketones.

reagents.name: mCPBA (meta-Chloroperoxybenzoic Acid)
reagents.function: Electrophilic peroxyacid; delivers oxygen across alkenes in syn-stereochemistry to yield epoxides (oxiranes); also performs Baeyer-Villiger oxidations.

reagents.name: SOCl2 (Thionyl Chloride / Pyridine)
reagents.function: Converts alcohols to alkyl chlorides with inversion of configuration via SN2 (with pyridine) or retention via SNi (without base); converts carboxylic acids to acyl chlorides.

reagents.name: PBr3 (Phosphorus Tribromide)
reagents.function: Converts 1° and 2° alcohols to alkyl bromides with clean Walden inversion of stereochemistry without carbocation rearrangement.

reagents.name: PCl5 (Phosphorus Pentachloride)
reagents.function: Replaces hydroxyl (-OH) or carbonyl oxygen (=O) with chlorine atoms; converts carboxylic acids to acid chlorides and ketones to gem-dichlorides.

reagents.name: TsCl / Pyridine (p-Toluenesulfonyl Chloride)
reagents.function: Converts poor leaving groups (-OH) into excellent sulfonate leaving groups (-OTs) with complete retention of configuration at carbon.
reagents.example: ROH + TsCl / pyridine -> ROTs + Pyridinium HCl

reagents.name: Lindlar's Catalyst (Pd/CaCO3 poisoned with Pb(OAc)2/Quinoline)
reagents.function: Selectively hydrogenates internal alkynes to cis-(Z)-alkenes via stereospecific syn-addition of H2 without reducing to alkanes.

reagents.name: Na in liquid NH3 (Birch Alkyne Reduction)
reagents.function: Dissolving metal reduction; selectively reduces internal alkynes to trans-(E)-alkenes via radical-anion anti-addition mechanism.

reagents.name: DIBAL-H (Diisobutylaluminium Hydride at -78°C)
reagents.function: Sterically hindered reducing agent; selectively reduces esters and nitriles to aldehydes at low temperature without over-reducing to alcohols/amines.

reagents.name: Grignard Reagent (RMgX in anhydrous ether)
reagents.function: Strong organometallic nucleophile/base; attacks carbonyls (formaldehyde -> 1° alcohol, aldehydes -> 2° alcohol, ketones/esters -> 3° alcohol).

reagents.name: Gilman Reagent (R2CuLi - Lithium Dialkylcuprate)
reagents.function: Organocuprate nucleophile; performs Corey-House cross-coupling with alkyl halides and 1,4-conjugate addition (Michael-type) on α,β-unsaturated enones.

reagents.name: Wittig Reagent (Phosphorus Ylide / Ph3P=CHR)
reagents.function: Converts aldehydes and ketones into alkenes with specific double-bond placement via an oxaphosphetane 4-membered cyclic transition state.

reagents.name: NBS (N-Bromosuccinimide / hν or peroxide)
reagents.function: Maintains low, constant concentration of Br2 for selective allylic and benzylic free-radical bromination without electrophilic addition across double bonds.

reagents.name: Lucas Reagent (Anhydrous ZnCl2 in concentrated HCl)
reagents.function: Diagnostic reagent for differentiating alcohols: 3° alcohols react immediately (turbidity < 1 min), 2° in 5 mins, 1° do not react at room temperature.

reagents.name: Tollens' Reagent (Ammoniacal Silver Nitrate / [Ag(NH3)2]+ OH-)
reagents.function: Mild oxidant specific for aldehydes; oxidises aliphatic and aromatic aldehydes to carboxylates with deposition of a shiny silver mirror (Ag(s)).

reagents.name: Fehling's Solution (Fehling A: CuSO4 + Fehling B: Tartrate in NaOH)
reagents.function: Diagnostic test for aliphatic aldehydes and reducing sugars; produces a bright red precipitate of cuprous oxide (Cu2O).

reagents.name: Benedict's Reagent (CuSO4 + Sodium Citrate + Na2CO3)
reagents.function: Qualitative test for aliphatic aldehydes and reducing carbohydrates; safer one-pot alternative to Fehling's, forming brick-red Cu2O precipitate.
reagents.example: Glucose + Benedict's reagent (heat) -> Red/Orange precipitate of Cu2O

reagents.name: 2,4-DNP / Brady's Reagent (2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine)
reagents.function: Diagnostic test for carbonyl groups (both aldehydes and ketones); forms yellow, orange, or red crystalline hydrazone precipitates with sharp melting points.

reagents.name: Diazomethane (CH2N2 in dry ether)
reagents.function: Mild methylating agent; quantitatively converts carboxylic acids into methyl esters with evolution of N2 gas; also converts acid chlorides to α-diazoketones (Arndt-Eistert).

reagents.name: LDA (Lithium Diisopropylamide at -78°C in THF)
reagents.function: Strong, sterically hindered, non-nucleophilic base; selectively deprotonates the less-hindered α-position of unsymmetrical ketones to form kinetic enolates.

reagents.name: KOtBu (Potassium tert-Butoxide in t-BuOH)
reagents.function: Bulky non-nucleophilic strong base; drives E2 dehydrohalogenation toward the least substituted, less hindered Hofmann alkene product.

reagents.name: Clemmensen Reagent (Amalgamated Zinc / conc. HCl)
reagents.function: Reduces aldehyde and ketone carbonyl groups directly into methylene (-CH2-) units under strongly acidic conditions; ideal for acid-stable substrates.
reagents.example: PhCOCH2CH3 + Zn(Hg) / conc. HCl -> PhCH2CH2CH3 + H2O

reagents.name: Wolff-Kishner Reagent (NH2NH2 + KOH in Ethylene Glycol / heat)
reagents.function: Reduces aldehyde and ketone carbonyls into methylene (-CH2-) groups under strongly basic conditions via hydrazone decomposition with N2 loss; ideal for acid-sensitive substrates.
reagents.example: Cyclohexanone + NH2NH2 / KOH, glycol (200°C) -> Cyclohexane + N2

reagents.name: HI in the presence of Red Phosphorus (Red P + HI)
reagents.function: Extremely powerful universal reducing agent at 150-200°C; reduces alcohols, aldehydes, ketones, and carboxylic acids completely into corresponding alkanes.
reagents.example: CH3COOH + Red P / HI (heat) -> CH3CH3 + 2 I2 + 2 H2O

reagents.name: Anhydrous AlCl3 (Aluminium Trichloride)
reagents.function: Potent Lewis acid catalyst; abstracts halide ions from alkyl/acyl halides to generate carbocations or acylium ions in electrophilic aromatic substitutions.

reagents.name: Nitrating Mixture (Concentrated HNO3 + Concentrated H2SO4)
reagents.function: Generates the powerful electrophilic nitronium ion (NO2+) for electrophilic aromatic nitration of benzene rings.

reagents.name: Br2 in FeBr3 (or Fe powder)
reagents.function: Lewis acid-activated halogenation system; polarises Br-Br to produce an electrophilic bromonium-like complex for aromatic bromination.

reagents.name: Periodic Acid (HIO4 / Malaprade Reagent)
reagents.function: Selectively cleaves vicinal diols (1,2-glycols) and α-hydroxy carbonyl compounds oxidatively with preservation of remainder of molecule.

reagents.name: Nitrous Acid (NaNO2 + aqueous HCl at 0-5°C)
reagents.function: Diazotises primary aromatic amines to stable aryl diazonium salts (ArN2+ Cl-); converts primary aliphatic amines to unstable diazoniums yielding alcohols/alkenes.
reagents.example: Aniline (PhNH2) + NaNO2 / HCl (0-5°C) -> Benzenediazonium chloride (PhN2+ Cl-)

reagents.name: Sandmeyer Reagent (Cu2Cl2 / HCl, Cu2Br2 / HBr, Cu2(CN)2 / KCN)
reagents.function: Replaces the diazonium group (-N2+) on aromatic rings with Cl, Br, or CN via a copper(I)-mediated radical-nucleophilic substitution.
reagents.example: PhN2+ Cl- + Cu2Cl2 / HCl -> Chlorobenzene (PhCl) + N2

reagents.name: Raney Nickel (Finely divided Ni-Al alloy treated with NaOH)
reagents.function: Porous catalyst loaded with adsorbed hydrogen; rapidly hydrogenates alkenes, alkynes, aromatic rings, and performs desulfurisation of thioacetals (Mozingo reaction).
reagents.example: Benzene + 3 H2 / Raney Ni (heat, pressure) -> Cyclohexane

named_reactions.name: Aldol Condensation
named_reactions.reactants: Aldehydes or ketones bearing α-hydrogen atoms treated with dilute alkali (NaOH, KOH) or acid, followed by heating.
named_reactions.products: α,β-Unsaturated aldehydes or ketones formed via dehydration of intermediate β-hydroxy carbonyl compounds.

named_reactions.name: Cannizzaro Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Non-enolisable aldehydes (no α-hydrogens: Formaldehyde, Benzaldehyde, Trimethylacetaldehyde) with concentrated 50% alkali.
named_reactions.products: Equimolar self-redox disproportionation mixture of a primary alcohol and a carboxylic acid salt.

named_reactions.name: Crossed Aldol Condensation
named_reactions.reactants: Two distinct carbonyl compounds, typically one lacking α-hydrogens (e.g., Benzaldehyde) and one with α-hydrogens (e.g., Acetaldehyde).
named_reactions.products: Single predominant conjugated α,β-unsaturated product (e.g., Cinnamaldehyde) due to selective enolate formation and electrophilicity.

named_reactions.name: Perkin Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Aromatic aldehyde + Aliphatic acid anhydride in the presence of the sodium/potassium salt of the corresponding acid at 180°C.
named_reactions.products: α,β-Unsaturated aromatic carboxylic acid (e.g., Benzaldehyde + Acetic anhydride/CH3COONa -> Cinnamic acid).

named_reactions.name: Benzoin Condensation
named_reactions.reactants: Two moles of aromatic aldehyde treated with catalytic cyanide ion (NaCN/KCN) in aqueous ethanol.
named_reactions.products: α-Hydroxy ketone / Aromatic acyloin (e.g., 2 PhCHO + NaCN -> Benzoin: Ph-CH(OH)-CO-Ph).

named_reactions.name: Wittig Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Aldehyde or ketone + Triphenylphosphonium ylide (Ph3P=CR2) in aprotic solvent.
named_reactions.products: Alkene with unambiguous double-bond regiochemistry + Triphenylphosphine oxide (Ph3P=O) byproduct.

named_reactions.name: Diels-Alder Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Conjugated diene in s-cis conformation + Electron-deficient dienophile under thermal [4+2] cycloaddition conditions.
named_reactions.products: Substituted cyclohexene derivative formed with high endo-stereoselectivity and retention of diene/dienophile configuration.

named_reactions.name: Friedel-Crafts Alkylation
named_reactions.reactants: Benzene or activated aromatic ring + Alkyl halide in the presence of anhydrous Lewis acid (AlCl3, FeCl3).
named_reactions.products: Alkylarene + HX (susceptible to carbocation rearrangement and polyalkylation).

named_reactions.name: Friedel-Crafts Acylation
named_reactions.reactants: Aromatic ring + Acyl halide or acid anhydride in the presence of anhydrous AlCl3.
named_reactions.products: Aryl ketone + HX (no carbocation rearrangement; deactivates ring against polyacylation).

named_reactions.name: Clemmensen Reduction
named_reactions.reactants: Aldehyde or ketone carbonyl + Amalgamated Zinc (Zn-Hg) in concentrated hydrochloric acid (HCl).
named_reactions.products: Alkane / Methylene compound (C=O -> CH2) without affecting unreactive functional groups stable to strong acid.

named_reactions.name: Wolff-Kishner Reduction
named_reactions.reactants: Aldehyde or ketone + Hydrazine (NH2NH2) and strong base (KOH) in high-boiling solvent (diethylene glycol) at 180-200°C.
named_reactions.products: Alkane + Nitrogen gas (N2) via hydrazone intermediate under basic conditions.

named_reactions.name: Rosenmund Reduction
named_reactions.reactants: Acyl chloride + H2 gas over palladium catalyst supported on BaSO4 and poisoned with quinoline/sulfur.
named_reactions.products: Aldehyde (prevented from over-reducing to primary alcohol by catalyst poison) + HCl.

named_reactions.name: Stephen Reduction
named_reactions.reactants: Alkyl or aryl nitrile + Anhydrous Stannous Chloride (SnCl2) and HCl gas, followed by steam hydrolysis of aldimine salt.
named_reactions.products: Aldehyde (RCHO) + NH4Cl.

named_reactions.name: Etard Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Toluene or alkylbenzene + Chromyl chloride (CrO2Cl2) in CS2 or CCl4, followed by aqueous decomposition.
named_reactions.products: Aromatic aldehyde (Benzaldehyde) without over-oxidation to benzoic acid via a brown chromium complex.

named_reactions.name: Gatterman-Koch Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Benzene or alkylbenzene + Carbon monoxide (CO) and hydrogen chloride (HCl) gas in the presence of anhydrous AlCl3 and CuCl.
named_reactions.products: Benzaldehyde or p-alkylbenzaldehyde via in situ formyl cation equivalent [H-C≡O]+.

named_reactions.name: Reimer-Tiemann Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Phenol + Chloroform (CHCl3) in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide (NaOH) at 60-70°C, followed by acidification.
named_reactions.products: Salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) as major ortho product via dichlorocarbene (:CCl2) intermediate.

named_reactions.name: Kolbe-Schmitt Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Sodium phenoxide (PhONa) + Carbon dioxide (CO2) gas under pressure (4-7 atm) at 125°C, followed by acidification.
named_reactions.products: Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) as major product due to sodium chelation in the transition state.

named_reactions.name: Williamson Ether Synthesis
named_reactions.reactants: Sodium alkoxide or phenoxide (RONa / ArONa) + Unhindered primary alkyl halide (R'X via SN2).
named_reactions.products: Unsymmetrical or symmetrical ether (R-O-R' / Ar-O-R') + NaX.

named_reactions.name: Hoffmann Bromamide Degradation
named_reactions.reactants: Primary carboxamide (RCONH2) + Bromine (Br2) in aqueous or ethanolic NaOH/KOH.
named_reactions.products: Primary amine (RNH2) having one fewer carbon atom + Na2CO3 + 2 NaBr + 2 H2O via isocyanate intermediate.

named_reactions.name: Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis
named_reactions.reactants: Potassium phthalimide + Primary alkyl halide (SN2), followed by hydrazine (NH2NH2) or alkaline hydrolysis.
named_reactions.products: Pure primary aliphatic amine (RNH2) strictly free from secondary or tertiary amine contaminants + Phthalhydrazide.

named_reactions.name: Sandmeyer Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Aryl diazonium salt (ArN2+ X-) + Cuprous halide/cyanide (Cu2Cl2/HCl, Cu2Br2/HBr, Cu2(CN)2/KCN).
named_reactions.products: Aryl halide or benzonitrile (ArCl, ArBr, ArCN) + Nitrogen gas (N2).

named_reactions.name: Gattermann Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Aryl diazonium salt + Copper powder (Cu) in the presence of halogen acid (HCl or HBr).
named_reactions.products: Aryl chloride or aryl bromide (ArCl, ArBr) + N2 (milder variant of Sandmeyer with lower yield).

named_reactions.name: Balz-Schiemann Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Aryl diazonium chloride + Fluoroboric acid (HBF4) to isolate diazonium fluoroborate precipitate, followed by dry heating.
named_reactions.products: Aryl fluoride (ArF) + Boron trifluoride (BF3) + N2 (safest route to fluoroarenes).

named_reactions.name: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Carboxylic acid containing α-hydrogens + Bromine or Chlorine in the presence of catalytic Red Phosphorus.
named_reactions.products: α-Halocarboxylic acid (e.g., CH3COOH + Br2/Red P -> BrCH2COOH) via enol acyl bromide intermediate.

named_reactions.name: Wurtz Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Two moles of alkyl halide (preferably primary) + Metallic Sodium in dry ether.
named_reactions.products: Symmetrical alkane containing twice as many carbons (2 R-X + 2 Na -> R-R + 2 NaX).

named_reactions.name: Fittig Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Two moles of aryl halide (ArX) + Metallic Sodium in dry ether.
named_reactions.products: Diaryl / Biphenyl (Ar-Ar) + 2 NaX.

named_reactions.name: Wurtz-Fittig Reaction
named_reactions.reactants: Equimolar mixture of an alkyl halide and an aryl halide + Metallic Sodium in dry ether.
named_reactions.products: Alkylarene (Ar-R) + 2 NaX.

named_reactions.name: Pinacol-Pinacolone Rearrangement
named_reactions.reactants: Vicinal tertiary diol (Pinacol: 2,3-dimethylbutane-2,3-diol) treated with concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4).
named_reactions.products: tert-Alkyl ketone (Pinacolone: 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-one) via carbocation formation and 1,2-methyl shift.

named_reactions.name: Beckmann Rearrangement
named_reactions.reactants: Ketoxime (derived from ketone + hydroxylamine) treated with acid catalyst (H2SO4, PCl5, SOCl2).
named_reactions.products: N-Substituted amide via stereospecific anti-migration of the group trans to the oxime hydroxyl group.

named_reactions.name: Baeyer-Villiger Oxidation
named_reactions.reactants: Ketone + Peroxyacid (mCPBA, trifluoroperacetic acid / CF3COOOH) in non-nucleophilic solvent.
named_reactions.products: Ester (or cyclic lactone from cyclic ketone) via oxygen insertion adjacent to the more substituted carbon.

basic_rules.definition: In electrophilic addition of an unsymmetrical polar reagent (H-X) to an unsymmetrical alkene, the proton adds to the double-bonded carbon bearing the greater number of hydrogen atoms, yielding the more stable carbocation intermediate.

In the presence of organic peroxides (ROOR) and light, addition of HBr (only HBr) proceeds via a free-radical chain mechanism where Br• adds to the less substituted carbon to generate the more stable alkyl radical.

In β-elimination reactions (E1 and unhindered E2) of alkyl halides or alcohols, the predominant alkene product is the most substituted and thermodynamically stable alkene (greatest number of alkyl substituents on the double bond).

In E2 eliminations involving bulky leaving groups (quaternary ammonium salts) or bulky bases (KOtBu), steric hindrance forces deprotonation of the least hindered β-hydrogen, yielding the least substituted (Hofmann) alkene.

A planar, monocyclic, continuously conjugated ring system possesses special thermodynamic stability (aromaticity) if it contains (4n + 2) π-electrons, where n is a non-negative integer (0, 1, 2, 3...). Rings with 4n π-electrons are anti-aromatic.

Atoms attached to a stereocenter or double bond are ranked by atomic number (higher Z = higher priority; isotopes by mass; multiple bonds counted as duplicated atoms) to unambiguously assign (R)/(S) stereocenters and (E)/(Z) alkene configurations.

A double bond cannot be positioned at the bridgehead position of a small or medium bridged bicyclic ring system (rings < 8 carbons) because the geometry prevents the required parallel p-orbital overlap, causing extreme angle strain.

Every concerted bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) reaction proceeds with 100% stereochemical inversion at the carbon reaction centre because the nucleophile must attack from the back face, 180° opposite the departing leaving group.

Pericyclic reactions (electrocyclic, cycloadditions, sigmatropic) proceed via concerted transition states that are symmetry-allowed only when orbital symmetry is preserved throughout the reaction coordinate under thermal or photochemical activation.

The transition state of an elementary reaction step resembles the species (reactants or products or intermediate) to which it is closer in free energy. In endergonic steps, the transition state closely resembles the unstable intermediate/product.

Predicts the diastereoselective outcome of nucleophilic attack on a chiral α-asymmetric carbonyl compound based on the conformational orientation of large (L), medium (M), and small (S) groups relative to the carbonyl plane.

A set of stereoelectronic guidelines classifying ring-closing reactions by ring size (3 to 7), hybridisation of the attacked carbon (tet, trig, dig), and bond location (exo vs endo) to determine whether the reaction is geometrically favoured or disfavoured.

Deprotonation of unsymmetrical ketones with a strong, bulky base (LDA) at -78°C gives the rapidly formed kinetic enolate (least substituted); deprotonation with small base (NaOEt) at equilibrium temperatures gives the more stable thermodynamic enolate.

For rapidly equilibrating conformational isomers that react irreversibly to give distinct products, the product ratio does not depend on the ground-state conformational equilibrium, but solely on the free-energy difference between their respective transition states.

Concerted bimolecular elimination requires the β-hydrogen, the two carbon atoms, and the leaving group to lie in the same plane with an anti-dihedral angle of 180° (anti-periplanar) to allow seamless overlap between the σ(C-H) and σ*(C-X) orbitals into the new π-bond.

core_concepts.details: Permanent polarisation of σ-bonds caused by electronegativity differences between bonded atoms. Electron-withdrawing groups (-I: -NO2, -CN, -F, -Cl, -COOH) stabilise conjugate bases and increase carboxylic acid strength; electron-donating groups (+I: alkyl groups) stabilise carbocations. The effect attenuates rapidly over 3 σ-bonds.

Delocalisation of π-electrons and lone pairs across conjugated systems through overlapping p-orbitals. Groups with lone pairs directly attached to the system (+M: -OH, -NH2, -OCH3) donate electron density into the ring/alkene; groups with polarised multiple bonds (-M: -NO2, -CHO, -CN) withdraw electron density by resonance.

Delocalisation of σ-electrons from C-H or C-C bonds into an adjacent empty, half-filled p-orbital or π* orbital (no-bond resonance). Governs the stability order of carbocations (3° > 2° > 1° > methyl), alkyl radicals, and substituted alkenes (more α-hydrogens = greater stability).

Aromatic compounds are cyclic, planar, fully conjugated with (4n + 2) π-electrons, having large resonance stabilisation. Anti-aromatic compounds are cyclic, planar, fully conjugated with 4n π-electrons, exhibiting severe electronic instability. Non-aromatic compounds lack planarity, cyclicity, or full conjugation (e.g., tub-shaped COT).

Carbocations are planar sp2 trivalent carbon cations stabilised by hyperconjugation and resonance (Tropylium > Triphenylmethyl > Benzyl/Allyl > 3° > 2° > 1° > Methyl > Vinyl). Secondary or primary carbocations spontaneously undergo 1,2-hydride, 1,2-methyl, or ring-expansion shifts (Wagner-Meerwein) to achieve higher stability.

Carbanions possess an unshared pair of electrons in an sp3 or sp hybrid orbital. Stability increases with higher s-character (sp [acetylide 50% s] > sp2 [phenyl 33% s] > sp3 [alkyl 25% s]) and when adjacent to electron-withdrawing groups (-M/-I) such as carbonyls (enolate stabilisation), nitro, or cyano groups.

core_concepts.concept: Free Radical Stability and Allylic/Benzylic Resonance
core_concepts.details: Neutral trivalent carbon intermediates with an unpaired electron in an sp2/sp3 orbital. Stabilised by resonance delocalisation across adjacent double bonds or aromatic rings (Benzylic > Allylic > 3° > 2° > 1° > Methyl > Vinyl). Formed homolytically by heat, UV light (hν), or peroxides.

Basicity is a thermodynamic measure of proton affinity (equilibrium constant Ka); nucleophilicity is a kinetic measure of carbon attack rate. In polar aprotic solvents (DMSO, DMF, acetone), nucleophilicity parallels basicity (F- > Cl- > Br- > I-). In polar protic solvents (H2O, MeOH), strong hydrogen bonding shells invert halide nucleophilicity (I- > Br- > Cl- > F-).

The ability of an atom or group to depart with an electron pair in substitution/elimination. Directly correlates with the thermodynamic stability of the departing anion (weaker conjugate base = better leaving group): TsO- ≈ TfO- > I- > Br- > Cl- >> F- > OH- > NH2- > OR-.

SN2 is a one-step concerted bimolecular substitution with rate = k[Substrate][Nu], favoured by 1° alkyl halides, strong nucleophiles, and polar aprotic solvents, yielding complete Walden inversion. SN1 is a two-step unimolecular substitution via carbocation with rate = k[Substrate], favoured by 3° halides, weak nucleophiles, and protic solvents, producing racemisation.

core_concepts.concept: E1 vs E2 vs E1cB Elimination Mechanisms
core_concepts.details: E2 is a concerted bimolecular elimination requiring anti-periplanar geometry and strong base. E1 is a two-step unimolecular elimination via carbocation intermediate under solvolytic/acidic conditions. E1cB involves deprotonation to a resonance-stabilised carbanion followed by slow expulsion of a poor leaving group (e.g., Aldol dehydration).

Substituents alter benzene reactivity by inductive and resonance effects. Strongly activating ortho/para directors (-OH, -NH2, -NR2) accelerate attack; alkyl groups (+I/hyperconjugation) are weak o/p directors. Deactivating meta directors (-NO2, -CN, -COOH, -CHO) pull electrons out of the ring. Halogens (-X) are deactivating yet ortho/para directing due to lone-pair resonance (+M > -I for regiochemistry, -I > +M for rate).

core_concepts.concept: Steric Hindrance and Transition State Conformations
core_concepts.details: Non-bonding spatial repulsion between electron clouds of bulky adjacent groups. Increases activation energies for backside attacks (making neopentyl halides unreactive in SN2) and forces reactions to proceed through less-congested transition states (e.g., Hofmann elimination with bulky KOtBu or 2,6-lutidine).

core_concepts.concept: Chirality, Optical Activity, Enantiomers, and Diastereomers
core_concepts.details: Chiral molecules lack an internal plane (σ) or inversion centre (i) of symmetry and rotate plane-polarised light. Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images with identical physical properties (except sign of optical rotation). Diastereomers are non-mirror image stereoisomers (including cis/trans and meso pairs) having different melting points, boiling points, and chemical reactivities.

Dynamic chemical equilibrium between a carbonyl compound (keto form) and an unsaturated alcohol (enol form) via α-proton migration. The keto form is thermodynamically favoured for simple aldehydes and ketones due to the strong C=O bond (~745 kJ/mol), but the enol form predominates in β-dicarbonyls (acetylacetone 80% enol) due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding and extended conjugation.
